extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department faculty, MER organizers, higher-education researchers and administrators interested in mathematics education reform
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and measures for assessing a research-oriented university mathematics department's engagement with, support for, and sustainability of mathematics education reform activities. Covers attitudes, faculty involvement, time allocation, institutional rewards, demographics, curricular reforms, and network participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental valuation of mathematics education reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Involvement in mathematics education reform is highly valued in my department. (Respondents rated agreement: Strongly Disagree / Tend to Disagree / Tend to Agree / Strongly Agree.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an attitudinal measure of whether reform is seen as important by the department. Table 13 presents responses across the agreement scale. A department scoring toward 'Tend to Agree'/'Strongly Agree' indicates higher institutional valuation; low scores indicate reform is peripheral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental atmosphere of acceptance and support for reform
rubrics_metrics.description: In my department, the atmosphere toward mathematics education reform is one of acceptance and support. (Same 4-point agreement scale.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses collegial and cultural receptivity beyond simple valuation. Positive atmosphere suggests easier implementation and faculty collaboration; negative atmosphere signals resistance and possible isolation of reform efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in departmental attitude toward reform over time
rubrics_metrics.description: During the past five years, the atmosphere in my department toward mathematics education reform has changed, becoming more positive towards it. (4-point agreement scale.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks momentum and trend: departments reporting positive change may be more likely to sustain reforms. Useful for longitudinal evaluation of intervention impact (e.g., MER workshops).

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental support for new projects and programs
rubrics_metrics.description: During the past five years, new projects and programs related to mathematics education have been supported by my department. (4-point agreement scale.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures concrete departmental backing (approval, resources, endorsement) for initiatives. High endorsement indicates institutional willingness to sponsor or adopt reform activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of faculty involved in K–12 math education reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of faculty involved in K-12 Math Education Reform (categories: 0%, 1–20%, 21–40%, 41–60%, 61–80%, 81–99%, 100%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 14 reports distributions (e.g., 64.1% of departments reported 1–20% involvement). Use to compare extent of outreach to pre-college education; low percentages indicate limited departmental engagement in K–12 reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of faculty involved in undergraduate math-education reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of faculty involved in undergraduate Math-Ed Reform (same categorical bands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as having higher involvement than many other educational activities but often still small (e.g., only 14% indicated >60% involvement). Useful for gauging internal curricular reform capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of faculty involved in teacher preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of faculty involved in Teacher Preparation (categories as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates department responsibility for pre-service teacher content and methods. High involvement implies substantial role in shaping future teachers; low involvement suggests reliance on other units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of faculty involved in reform of graduate education for mathematics students
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of faculty involved in Reform of Graduate Education — for Mathematics Students (categorical bands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 14 shows many departments have low faculty involvement in graduate education reform; use to assess attention to graduate curriculum changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of faculty involved in reform of graduate education for math-education students
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of faculty involved in Reform of Graduate Education — for Math-Education Students (categorical bands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often the fewest faculty are involved here (e.g., large percentage at 0%). Highlights where departments are least active and potential targets for MER support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of faculty involved in teacher in-service activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of faculty involved in Teacher In-Service Activities (categorical bands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate outreach and professional development engagement with in-service teachers; Table 14 reports most responses clustered at 1–20% involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of faculty active in mathematics research
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of faculty involved in Mathematics Research (categorical bands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a baseline contrast to educational activities (e.g., 44% of respondents reported >60% of faculty involved in research). Useful to understand departmental mission weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment between actual time spent and perceived departmental expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: How respondents distributed their time compared to their perceptions of how their institution expected them to spend their time across activities (teaching, research/scholarship, math education reform, service, administration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures congruence or mismatch: e.g., many reported spending less time on research than their institution expects and more time on reform/service/admin than expected; teaching time roughly matched expectations. Useful for diagnosing reward-structure misalignments that threaten sustainability of reform activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total hours worked per week
rubrics_metrics.description: Total hours worked/week (bands: <40, 40–49, 50–59, 60–69, >70) and mean/std. dev.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides workload context for time-allocation measures (majority reported >50 hours/week). High workloads can constrain faculty ability to engage in reform or sustain additional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional reward structures for educational involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent institutional support includes rewards for educational involvement such as consideration in promotion and tenure decisions, release time for educational involvement, becoming more respectful of educational involvement and general administrative support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete indicators of institutional support: promotion/tenure consideration, release time, official recognition, hiring/promotion for education work, designated faculty development time, faculty development workshops. Presence/absence is a key predictor of whether reform activities are sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimization of mathematics education reform within the research community
rubrics_metrics.description: The Forum legitimizes mathematics education reform within the mathematics research community (e.g., 'Affecting positively mathematics education reform mainly by legitimizing mathematics education and get rid of its second-class status.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soft institutional metric: increased respectability and social acceptability among research mathematicians. Helps participants feel empowered to push for changes and to return to campuses with legitimacy; measured qualitatively via testimonials and perceived influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental culture and structural features supporting sustained reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Models of departments in which the departmental culture promotes regular, thoughtful study of its educational responsibilities are needed. Critiques of existing models include reliance on two-tiered faculty structures, projects seen as 'Professor X's project', and the persistence of a dichotomy between mathematics education and mathematics research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key features of successful departmental models: educational goals integral to mission, broadly based faculty participation, unified purpose, intellectual discourse, and commitment. Anti-patterns: isolated initiatives, dependence on adjuncts or single champions, and protectionist research culture that marginalizes education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic representation and retention metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty and student demographics: percent women and minorities among tenure-track and full-time faculty, percent female and minority graduate students, retention/completion rates for Ph.D. programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks and concerns: faculty often over-represent white men (women ~5–10% of tenure-track in sample), females much better represented among graduate students, minority representation low but higher at undergraduate level in some sites. Retention rates ~40–50% cited. Use demographic percentages and retention as equity and pipeline health indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental role in pre-service teacher preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the mathematics department is responsible for mathematics content courses and methods courses for pre-service teachers (varies across institutions; some have a mathematics major for pre-service secondary teachers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates formal curricular responsibility: if department teaches methods and content for teachers, it has greater leverage over teacher preparation. Use existence of majors/concentrations and course assignments as indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability of special programs beyond founders
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether special programs are regarded as departmental responsibility or as 'Professor X's project' and thus unlikely to survive without the founder's involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational sustainability indicator: programs embedded in departmental structures and shared among faculty are more durable than founder-dependent initiatives. Use governance, staffing plans, and evidence of broad participation to assess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in networks and workshops as dissemination and support mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments' and individuals' attendance at MER workshops and use of network-sharing (e.g., Santa Barbara workshop) to exchange experiences and influence departmental decisions (e.g., adoption of Harvard Calculus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures external engagement and diffusion of ideas. Evidence of impact includes faculty citing other departments' experiences to justify reforms and adoption of practices after workshop attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption and implementation characteristics of undergraduate curriculum reform (including calculus reform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and nature of undergraduate curriculum reform (e.g., experimentation with Harvard Calculus, structural changes like class size and use of graphing calculators), including degrees of adoption and necessary local modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates not just adoption but implementation fidelity and contextual modification (budget constraints, staffing, coverage concerns). Use evidence of department-wide commitments, pilot sections, faculty deliberation, and structural changes (class size limits) as indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology in mathematics curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of technology into the mathematics curriculum (graphing calculators, mathematical software used by students and instructors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of pedagogical innovation. Degree of integration, instructor support/training, and availability of resources determine effectiveness; monitor concerns about staffing and faculty readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource constraints and structural barriers to reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of budgetary constraints, large class sizes, staffing limitations, and competing priorities that affect ability to implement reforms (e.g., inability to maintain smaller classes despite adoption of new materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual constraint metric: track how fiscal and staffing realities force modifications or limit reforms. Use class size data, resource allocation, and administrative commitments to assess feasibility and scalability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of qualifying exams and graduate admissions in diversity and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying exams are described as a difficult hurdle affecting graduate retention and selection; chairs noted reluctance to admit students who cannot pass qualifying exams, impacting minority recruitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exam difficulty and admission policies as evaluative levers affecting diversity and pipeline health; consider alternative supports or revisions if exams disproportionately hinder underrepresented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of department service to non-university community
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the department has institutional links to non-university community efforts (state initiatives, school districts, textbook committees) versus primarily individual faculty efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures institutional outreach capacity. Departments with formal links and supported community engagement are better positioned to influence K–12 and public understanding; absence suggests reliance on sporadic individual action.
